papers.title: Dedekind Eta Powers and Interlacing in Lambert Series Quotients
papers.abstract: For each $0<q<1$ we prove that the zeros and poles of a quotient of Lambert series formed from the cube of Euler's product are simple, negative and strictly interlacing. The zeros of the sampled series decrease strictly as its shift increases through $(0,1]$. The quotient has a partial-fraction expansion with positive weights, and every average over the $d$-th roots of unity with $d$ odd exceeds the value of the quotient at the origin. For even $d$, every pole of the average in the parameter $q\in(0,1)$ is simple and has positive residue. We also characterize the cube as the unique positive integer power of Euler's product whose sampling kernel is a P\'olya frequency function. For a general positive integer power $k$ and integer dilation $a\ge2$, the quotient interpolates $z^{1-1/a}$ at geometric nodes selected by the nonzero coefficients of the Euler product power. We determine its radial limit away from two real rays and the asymptotic locations of the poles of the averages of even order near $q=1$. For the cube, convergence to the fractional power is exponentially fast on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$. The positive discrete measures in the partial-fraction expansion converge vaguely on $(0,\infty)$ to $\pi^{-1}\sin(\pi/a)u^{-1/a}\,du$.
